text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Under a government pardon marking the country's national day, Kuwait releases 10 Jordanians from prison.
- Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti warns that an Israeli settlement drive in Jerusalem would affect the peace process.
- Jordanian detainees in Israeli jails begin a week-long hunger strike in protest at their continued detention.
- King Hussein gives instructions to boost the role of the bedouin army and border police after an inspection visit to army headquarters.
- Fifteen deputies table a motion for a session to debate employee salaries.
- King Hussein writes to Libyan leader Gaddafi calling for a boost to "brotherly" ties.
- Salvage teams continue search for missing girl feared drowned after being swept away by floods.
- U.S. grants Jordan $21 million soft loan to help finance purchase of 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat from private sources.
- A large embezzlement case by employees in the customs is said to have been discovered.
- A new system for calculating customs on cars to be introduced soon.
- King meets American friends of Israeli Mertz delegation, reaffirms commitment to peace.
- Jordan, Kuwait exchange greetings on Kuwait's national day.
